# Draft:Alexander Heritage and research facility

----
Alexander Heritage and Research Library (also referred to as the Alexander Heritage & Research Facility and Te Rerenga Mai o Te Kāuru) is a specialised library and research institution located in Whanganui, New Zealand. It functions as a repository for regional history, genealogy (whakapapa), and cultural heritage materials, supporting scholarly and public research into the historical record of Whanganui and surrounding communities.
The Alexander Heritage and Research Library traces its origins to the early 20th century. Its collection was established through donations, particularly from the Alexander family, and the facility formally opened in 1933. The heritage collection was developed to preserve books, historical documents, photographs, newspapers, military records, and other materials relevant to local history and familial research. The original building, designed by the architectural firm Hood & Duffell, remains an integral heritage structure in Whanganui’s Queen’s Park area. The library’s core mission is to collect, preserve, and provide access to records that document the people, organisations, events, and cultural narratives of Whanganui and nearby regions. Its holdings include local newspapers, rare books, photographs, pamphlets, and specialised archives such as military records. Patrons can access leading genealogy databases, including Ancestry Library and Find My Past, to facilitate family history research.
